review_notes: Reviewed the whole file (one iff lemma, one corollary) and grepped the repo for other ULift uses and for the simp setup in HurewiczFibration/Basic.lean. The only simp-relevant declaration is isHurewiczFibration_ulift_iff. I did not run Lean, so the claim about matching is based on the shape of the LHS, not on an experiment. The repo has no use of the lemma through `simp`; the only use found is `.mpr` at line 63.

findings.excerpt:
@[simp]
theorem isHurewiczFibration_ulift_iff :
    IsHurewiczFibration.{w}
      (fun e : ULift.{u'} E ↦ (ULift.up (p e.down) : ULift.{v'} B)) ↔
findings.problem: The `@[simp]` LHS is `IsHurewiczFibration (fun e => ULift.up (p e.down))`, where `p` is a variable. The LHS contains the term `?p e.down`, whose argument is not a bound variable, so it is not a higher-order pattern. The rule can only fire if the map is syntactically written as this exact lambda, up to a first-order guess for `?p`. Lifted maps are normally written with other forms, such as `ULift.map`, a composition `ULift.up ∘ p ∘ ULift.down`, or a bundled/`TopCat` hom. For those forms the rule does not apply, so it adds a simp lemma with a fragile match and little benefit. The lambda is also a lemma-specific normal form that the file never establishes as canonical. Nothing in the repo uses this lemma through `simp`; the only use is the explicit `.mpr` at line 63.
findings.proposed_change: Drop `@[simp]` and keep the lemma as an ordinary iff, used explicitly as at line 63. If a simp interface is wanted, first pick a canonical lifted-map form (for example `ULift.map p` if it is available, or `ULift.up ∘ p ∘ ULift.down`). State the iff for that form and tag that version. Also decide whether the other direction, the simp-normal form of `IsHurewiczFibration.{w} (ULift.up ∘ p ∘ ULift.down)`, should simplify to `IsHurewiczFibration.{w} p`.
findings.benefit: This avoids a simp lemma that silently fails to match the usual spellings of lifted maps. It also keeps the simp set free of an unmotivated lambda-shaped rule, and any future simp attribute would sit on an expression that actually occurs.
